candidates.notes: Li10 is a literature candidate from Li et al. (2015), not a new object introduced by this paper. The paper reassesses it with Gaia DR2 astrometry and a new SOAR/Goodman radial velocity, and treats it as the only known late-type hypervelocity star. Sec. 3.3 rules out a Galactic-centre Hills origin because the pericentric radius is 3.3 +/- 0.2 kpc, discusses runaway and halo radial-orbit interpretations, and reports no evidence for a close-binary radial-velocity shift.

notes: Draft based on the PDF only for blind annotation. The paper is a Gaia DR2 reassessment of historical high-velocity candidates, not a new unbound-HVS discovery paper. Its broad conclusion is that most historical late-type high-velocity candidates become bound with Gaia DR2, while early-type HVS candidates largely remain supported because their large radial velocities already established the HVS status. Table 1 lists P_bound < 0.5 candidates grouped by discovery source; this draft records the individually discussed remaining late-type candidate Li10 from Sec. 3.3 as cited_from_literature.
